disease_label_per_paper: Henoch-Schonlein purpura presenting as severe gastrointestinal and renal involvement with mixed outcomes in an adult patient
presentation_summary: A 48-year-old man with no past medical or surgical history except a 20-pack-year smoking history first developed one day of new lower-extremity purpuric rash with hand and foot swelling/soreness.
Initial examination showed stable vital signs, purpura with some pustular lesions over both lower extremities and suprapubic region, and bilateral hand/foot swelling.
Initial urine studies showed urine protein 203 mg/dL, 5-10 RBC/HPF, 2-5 hyaline casts/field, urine protein:creatinine ratio 859 mg/g, and serum creatinine 1.6 mg/dL.

Five days later he returned with coffee-ground emesis, melena, diffuse abdominal pain, persistent lower-extremity purpura, creatinine 2.4 mg/dL, albumin 1.6 g/dL, CRP 5.3 mg/dL, hematuria 25-50 RBC/HPF, and proteinuria 9 g/g.
Autoimmune/infectious workup including ANA, p-ANCA, c-ANCA, anti-GBM, complement levels, cryoglobulins, HIV, hepatitis panel, IgA levels, and SPEP was within normal limits.
Hemoglobin decreased from 15.5 g/dL to 11 g/dL over two days.
Pulse IV methylprednisolone 500 mg daily for three days was started, then IV methylprednisolone 60 mg twice daily; renal function worsened with creatinine to 3.70 mg/dL.

EGD showed esophagitis and severe patchy duodenal inflammation, erythema, edema, petechiae, ulceration, friability, and stigmata of recent bleeding suggestive of ischemia; sigmoidoscopy showed patchy rectosigmoid inflammation.

CT abdomen/pelvis showed severe pan-inflammation of the duodenum and colon, thickened small and large bowel walls, multiple dilated bowel loops, nonspecific periappendiceal inflammation/dilation, and ascites.
Renal biopsy showed proliferative and crescentic IgA-dominant glomerulonephritis; 4 of 7 glomeruli had epithelial crescents.

Cyclophosphamide was added, but ongoing hematemesis, hematochezia, abdominal pain, and renal failure progressed to peak creatinine 5.37 mg/dL requiring hemodialysis; plasmapheresis was started on alternating days with dialysis for eight sessions.
GI symptoms improved after escalation, but renal function did not recover and the patient required outpatient dialysis.

clinical_course.event: Initial lower-extremity purpura, hand/foot swelling and soreness, proteinuria, hematuria, and creatinine 1.6 mg/dL.
Returned with coffee-ground emesis, melena, diffuse abdominal pain, creatinine 2.4 mg/dL, albumin 1.6 g/dL, CRP 5.3 mg/dL, worsening hematuria and nephrotic-range proteinuria.
Renal biopsy and EGD/sigmoidoscopy performed; hemodialysis started.
Creatinine peaked at 5.37 mg/dL; ongoing hematemesis/hematochezia and abdominal pain led to plasmapheresis.
GI symptoms improved after escalation, but renal function did not recover.

outcome.source_text_value: Plasmapheresis resulted in improvement of gastrointestinal symptoms, but no recovery was seen of renal function, and the patient required outpatient dialysis.
